prompt.context: Our client is an online dating startup named Grad-U-Date, which specializes in matching graduate students with other graduate students. Grad-U-Date has finished building their app and are now looking for your assistance in deciding on a monetization strategy.
prompt.question: What is Grad-U-Date's best method of monetization? How profitable will the company be?

clarifying_info.q: What is the gender ratio of users?
clarifying_info.a: The gender ratio of users will be 50/50.
MBA, law, and medical students are considered professional students.

clarifying_info.q: Has the app already been built?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the app has already been built and is considered a sunk cost.
Grad-U-Date will only operate within the United States.
There are 4 major competitors and hundreds of small competitors.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other dating services focused on graduate students?
clarifying_info.a: No, there are currently no other online dating services that focus only on graduate students.

clarifying_info.q: Can Grad-U-Date use multiple revenue models?
clarifying_info.a: No, only one revenue model can be used.

exhibits.title: Student Enrolment Information
exhibits.shows: A bar chart and table showing new graduate students per university per year by program type, alongside the number of years required to complete each degree. There are 1,000 universities in the United States.

exhibits.title: Product Usage and Revenue Model Parameters
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the forecasted percentage of graduate students using Grad-U-Date under each monetization model (Monthly Fee: 5%, Premium Account: 30%, Advertising: 40%), along with pricing details for each model.

data.Premium account cost: $5 per month; 40% of men and 20% of women purchase premium accounts

exhibits.title: Online Dating Market Trends
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis line chart showing trends from 2008 to 2014 in the percentage of online dating users paying a monthly fee (left axis) and the average monthly fee paid in dollars (right axis). Both metrics decline sharply starting around 2012-2013.

data.Metrics: % users paying monthly fee (0–70% scale) and average monthly fee in dollars (0–70 scale)
data.Notable trend: Both metrics drop sharply beginning in 2013

framework: Market size: estimate the total addressable market of graduate students in the US
Competitive landscape / market share: assess major and small competitors and Grad-U-Date's positioning
Revenue model options: brainstorm and evaluate monetization models (monthly fee, advertising, premium account, etc.)
Profitability analysis: calculate revenue and profit for each viable model using fixed and variable costs
Recommendation: select the best revenue model based on profitability and market trends, identify risks and next steps

questions.prompt: What types of monetization models could Grad-U-Date use? What are the advantages and disadvantages of each?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm at least 3 (ideally 5+) models and remain structured. Strong candidates bucket the models and articulate clear pros and cons for each. Models to cover include: Monthly subscription fee (predictable revenue but limits user base), Advertising (large free user base, ad revenue per user), Premium account / freemium (free base with paid upgrades; broad user adoption), Profile consulting services, Micro-transactions (e.g., pay per message, profile bump), Pay-per-feature. For each, discuss trade-offs around adoption rate, revenue per user, and impact on user experience.

questions.prompt: Grad-U-Date is considering limiting the site to only MBA students. What issues might there be with an MBA-only dating website?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) Gender skew — more men than women at most MBA programs leading to an imbalanced platform; (2) Market size limitation — unnecessarily restricts total addressable market; (3) Demographic concerns — MBA students tend to be older and many are already married or in committed relationships, reducing the addressable user pool.

questions.prompt: What is the potential market size for Grad-U-Date? [Share Exhibit 1 with candidate]
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the enrollment data to calculate total graduate students enrolled at any given time (enrollment = new students per year x years for degree), then multiply by number of universities. Walk through the math systematically.

math.setup: For each program: enrolled students per university = new students per year x years for degree. Sum across programs = total grad students per university. Multiply by 1,000 universities.
math.answer: 6,000,000 graduate students in the United States

questions.prompt: Calculate the profit of each revenue model. Fixed costs are $10,000,000 a year and variable operating cost is $1 per member per year. Which revenue model would you recommend? [Provide Exhibit 2]
questions.guidance: Candidate must methodically compute customers, revenue, and profit for each model. Should use the 50/50 gender split and professional/non-professional split (3,000 professional out of 6,000 per university = 50%) from prior analysis. Monthly fee yields highest profit and should be the initial recommendation before Exhibit 3 is introduced.

math.setup: Fixed costs = $10,000,000/year; Variable cost = $1 per member per year. Use Exhibit 2 adoption rates and pricing. Gender ratio 50/50. Professional/non-professional split 50/50.
steps: Ad revenue per user: 50% professional x $1.25 + 50% non-professional x $0.75 = $0.625 + $0.375 = $1.00 per user per month
math.answer: Monthly Fee: $25,700,000 profit; Premium Account: $20,600,000 profit; Advertising: $16,400,000 profit. Monthly fee is most profitable before considering market trends.

questions.prompt: Does this information change your recommendation for which revenue model? [Provide Exhibit 3]
questions.guidance: Candidate should switch recommendation from monthly fee to premium account. Exhibit 3 shows that the percentage of users paying monthly fees and the average monthly fee have been declining sharply since 2012-2013, suggesting monthly fee revenue is likely unsustainable. Premium account model is more resilient and still profitable at $20,600,000.

questions.prompt: Why do you think that the percentage of users paying monthly fees dropped so quickly starting in 2013?
questions.guidance: Candidate should connect the trend to competitive dynamics: (1) Significant increase in the number of free dating apps starting in late 2012; (2) Launch of Tinder in late 2012, which introduced a high-quality free dating experience; (3) Increased overall competition in the online dating market making users less willing to pay fees.

brainstorming.prompt: Given your recommended revenue model (premium account), what other strategies can Grad-U-Date use to increase profit?

categories.name: Reduce Costs
ideas: Outsource servers to reduce infrastructure costs
Only provide email support and eliminate phone support to reduce headcount

categories.name: Increase Revenue
ideas: Create a mobile app to attract more customers and increase adoption
Offer profile consulting services as an add-on revenue stream
Partner with popular date locations to offer deals (affiliate/referral revenue)
Expand to recent graduate school alumni to extend the addressable market
Add micro-transactions such as paying to boost profile visibility (profile bump)
Incorporate social media integrations to drive organic growth
Explore whether premium account and advertising models can be combined

recommendation: Grad-U-Date should adopt the premium account revenue model
The monthly fee model should not be selected because this segment is rapidly disappearing (as shown by Exhibit 3) and it limits the number of users on the platform
The premium account model is expected to generate $20,600,000 in annual profit while supporting a larger free user base of 1,800,000
risks: Premium account adoption could be seeing a similar declining trend as the monthly fee model
A smaller percentage of users than forecast may choose to purchase a premium account
The ad-supported model could be growing faster than the premium account model, making it more attractive in future years
Graduate students may not be able to afford premium account fees
Number of people enrolling in graduate school could decrease, shrinking the addressable market
Graduate students may prefer not to limit their dating pool to other grad students, reducing adoption
next_steps: Research market trends for ad-supported and premium account revenue models to validate assumptions
Explore expansion into new markets such as undergraduates or international students
Offer additional services: profile consulting and partnerships with date-night venues
Add micro-transactions to create supplemental revenue within the premium model
Incorporate social media features to drive organic growth
Investigate whether a hybrid model (premium account + limited advertising) is feasible
